## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the swell period this break needs.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> All 4 readable current sources were re-read and 2 new ones added: hawaii.surf and Caldwell 2005 (JCR, region-wide season). WIND: Surf-Forecast SSE, hawaii.surf SSE, WannaSurf SE/E and WSL light easterly trades (NE gives side-shore texture) all fall within 45 deg of 135. Wikipedia calls the trades offshore without giving a direction (value null). SWELL DIRECTION: NW is consistent across Surf-Forecast, WSL and hawaii.surf (310-340, ideal 315-320). Wikipedia W-NE and WannaSurf N/NW/W are wider. All fit 300-350. SIZE CONFLICT: WSL 6-18 ft and WannaSurf from 3 ft (proper from 6 ft) fit the profile's 5-18, but hawaii.surf says faces over 25 ft are handled (plus the 403 SURFER, Surfertoday and GoHawaii claims of 20-30 ft), so the profile max of 18 looks low for the outer reef. Feet scales are inconsistent. PERIOD: first numeric support is hawaii.surf (14+ s best, 10-13 s choppier), a single community source. TIDE: WannaSurf all tides supports 'all'. hawaii.surf is section-dependent (low-mid for the Bowl, mid-high for the Point), so it was not recorded. WAVE DIRECTION CONFLICT: Surf-Forecast says 'Both left and right' and WSL mentions the left in NE wind, while WannaSurf and the profile say right. Not readable (403): Surfertoday, SURFER, GoHawaii (now magazine), T&F JEPM (Crossref shows a 2024 paper on coastal retreat with no abstract; kept unchanged). No measured bathymetry found.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–5 ft (1–1.5 m) [S4] · 4–6 ft [S9] · 6 ft [S5] (scale not stated) | conflicting | S4, S5, S9 | `wave_height_min_ft` 5 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 6–8 ft (scale not stated) | documented | S9 | no separate setting; working range 5–18 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 18 ft; scale: not stated [S5] · 16 ft (5 m) or more; scale: not stated [S4] · 25 ft or more; scale: face [S9] · 20–30 ft; scale: Hawaiian [S6] · 30 ft; scale: not stated (outer deep-water reef) [S3] · 30 ft; scale: not stated (promotional) [S8] | conflicting | S3, S4, S5, S6, S8, S9 | `wave_height_max_ft` 18 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft, hawaii.surf that Sunset Point starts at about 4-6 ft, and WSL that it breaks from six feet; none states whether these are faces or offshore swell heights.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S9 (hawaii.surf): “Sunset Point starts working around 4-6 feet and is optimal at 6-8 feet.”
  - S5 (World Surf League): “Drawing in west, northwest over a double finger of reef, this beast breaks anywhere from six to 18 feet.”
- **Ideal range**: hawaii.surf says Sunset Point is optimal at 6-8 feet, without stating the scale; it is the only source with an ideal size.
  - S9 (hawaii.surf): “Sunset Point starts working around 4-6 feet and is optimal at 6-8 feet.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WSL says it breaks up to 18 feet and WannaSurf that it holds 5 m / 16 ft and over, while hawaii.surf says it handles faces over 25 ft, SURFER (search summary) 20-30 ft Hawaiian scale, and Surfertoday and GoHawaii (search summaries) up to 30 ft; the scales differ and Hawaiian-scale heights are not converted because no source states the conversion.
  - S5 (World Surf League): “Drawing in west, northwest over a double finger of reef, this beast breaks anywhere from six to 18 feet.”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S9 (hawaii.surf): “Sunset can handle enormous swells exceeding 25 plus feet on the face”
  - S6 (SURFER): “When Pipeline maxes out, Sunset can hold 20-to-30-foot waves (Hawaiian scale).”
  - S3 (Surfertoday): “On big swell days, the outer deep-water reef pumps massive walls of fast-moving water that can easily get to 30 feet.”
  - S8 (GoHawaii.com (Hawaii tourism site)): “Winter is the big-wave season there, and the same page puts swells up to 30 feet tall.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft, hawaii.surf that Sunset Point starts at about 4-6 ft, and WSL that it breaks from six feet; none states whether these are faces or offshore swell heights.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: WSL says it breaks up to 18 feet and WannaSurf that it holds 5 m / 16 ft and over, while hawaii.surf says it handles faces over 25 ft, SURFER (search summary) 20-30 ft Hawaiian scale, and Surfertoday and GoHawaii (search summaries) up to 30 ft; the scales differ and Hawaiian-scale heights are not converted because no source states the conversion.
- **Swell direction · acceptable range**: Wikipedia says it works on west-to-northeast North Pacific swells and WannaSurf lists north, northwest and west, while hawaii.surf gives a narrower primary window of 310-340 deg; only Wikipedia includes northeast.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast and hawaii.surf name a south-southeast offshore, WannaSurf lists southeast and east as good winds, WSL says it does best with light easterly trades, and Wikipedia says the trade winds blow offshore without giving a direction.
